purpose: VibeVoice-ASR Q4_K_M decode: route rows=1 through the raw-block pack8 decode GEMV families
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 256-bit LPDDR5X, 133 GB unified

protocol.weights: Q4_K_M backbone (168 Q4_K + 28 Q6_K layer tensors), bf16 front-end + dense bf16 untied lm_head
protocol.kernels: gguf_q4_k_pack8_gemv_decode_* / gguf_q6_k_pack8_gemv_decode_* read the unmodified GGUF block bytes on device; no repack, no sidecar, no extra resident memory
protocol.workload: Qwen2 backbone decode at ~150-token context, 3 warmup steps, 3 timed trials of 40 steps; both lanes measured in one process, with the same loop, fixture and prompt rows
protocol.command: python3 - <<'EOF' (load /tmp/vibevoice-asr-q4km.gguf, prompt from tests/fixtures/vibevoice_asr/vibevoice_asr_lm.npz, time push_token+forward_layers+logits_argmax loops) EOF

results.prior_naive_source: worklog 20260914T111748.594243Z (recorded baseline, not re-measured in this session)

gates.gpu_suite: 7/7 tests/test_gpu_vibevoice_qwen2_q4_runner.py incl. greedy chain 16/16 vs torch fixture and first-position logits top-1
gates.weight_type_routing: all 196 layer GEMM weights still route to K-quant blocks the kernels own
gates.wer_recheck: PASS - 20-clip Q4 lane with the pack8 path: Q4 1.487% == bf16 1.487% on the same 20 clips, 0/20 per-clip WER differences, 18/20 transcripts byte-identical, 0 malformed transcripts

notes: The naive per-column raw-block GEMVs run at 18-60 GB/s; the pack8 decode families reach 107-132 GB/s, which is the bandwidth wall for these shapes.
The 5.01 GB/token stream is 3.92 GB of layer GEMM weights plus a 1.09 GB dense bf16 lm_head; the lm_head is ~6.6 ms of the ~48 ms and already runs at ~210 GB/s.

A single-GEMV speedup does not transfer one-for-one: the microbenchmark projected 39.1 ms/token and the integrated decode measures 48.1 ms (1.26x optimism) because of per-token non-GEMM work (196 GEMM launches plus ~336 norm/rotary/KV/attention/residual/silu launches) and context-dependent attention.
Prefill is unchanged and is the dominant remaining cost; see results_prefill for the route correction.

results_prefill.note: Both lanes were driven row-by-row (push_token + forward_layers) so this loop does NOT exercise the bf16 hipBLASLt batched prefill. It measures the row-by-row route only.
results_prefill.conclusion: Q4 has no batched prefill route at all, so the real deficit is against bf16's batched route: ~6.3 s vs ~0.30 s for a 146-row request. An earlier draft compared Q4's row-by-row time against bf16's batched time; that conflated two routes.
